blueprint_topic: Management of Care — safe transfer, direct clinical handoff, continuity of care, and transfer of responsibility
stem: An RN is transferring a postoperative client from the recovery area to an inpatient unit. Which action best demonstrates the RN's Management of Care responsibility during the transition?

options.A: Give the receiving nurse a direct handoff covering current status, treatment response, recent changes, and the care plan, with time for questions.
options.B: Complete the electronic transfer note and send the client once the bed is ready, expecting the receiving nurse to review the record before assuming care.
options.C: Ask the charge nurse to relay the transfer summary and have the receiving nurse contact the sending unit later if clarification is needed.
options.D: Report the procedures already completed and let the receiving nurse determine current concerns and pending needs after the client arrives.

rationale: A is correct. The current 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan identifies both safe client transfer and providing/receiving handoff of care as Management of Care responsibilities. Current AHRQ TeamSTEPPS guidance defines handoff as a standardized transfer of information, authority, and responsibility during transitions in care and states that handoffs include treatment response, recent changes in condition or circumstances, and the care plan including contingencies. AHRQ also emphasizes acknowledgment by the receiver and an opportunity for questions; electronic handoffs can support documentation but may be most effective when reinforced by direct communication. B is incorrect because documenting in the EHR does not by itself establish that responsibility and essential information have been received and understood. C is incorrect because indirect relay and delayed clarification weaken the direct transfer of information and responsibility. D is incomplete because a safe handoff includes the client's current condition, response, recent changes, and ongoing plan rather than only completed procedures.
educational_objective: Perform a safe transfer by providing a direct clinical handoff that communicates current status, treatment response, recent changes, and the ongoing care plan while confirming receipt of responsibility.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN); Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; TeamSTEPPS Tool: Handoff
source_version_date: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026; current AHRQ TeamSTEPPS Handoff resource rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, printed page 7 / PDF pageno 10: related activity statements include 'Perform procedures necessary to safely admit, transfer and/or discharge a client' and 'Provide and receive handoff of care (report) on assigned clients.' AHRQ TeamSTEPPS 'Tool: Handoff': a handoff transfers information, authority, and responsibility during transitions; information includes treatment response, recent changes in condition/circumstances, and the care plan including contingencies; effective handoff includes receiver acknowledgment and opportunity for questions, and electronic handoffs may be reinforced by direct communication.

pdf_visual_verification: PASS — the official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed page 7 / PDF pageno 10 was freshly screenshot-verified on 2026-08-20 and visibly contains the safe-transfer and handoff activity statements. AHRQ evidence is current HTML; no AHRQ PDF evidence is used.
correction_summary: Original Q1970 had a uniquely longest correct answer and distractors that simply denied the need for handoff. The item was rebuilt so each option describes a plausible transfer workflow. The correct answer now requires direct communication of clinically relevant transition information plus opportunity for receiver confirmation/questions, while distractors test overreliance on the EHR, indirect relay, or incomplete reporting.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches NCSBN's handoff responsibility and AHRQ's information-transfer, responsibility, and communication elements.
option_audit.B: Plausible EHR-reliance distractor; incorrect because documentation alone does not ensure direct transfer and acknowledgment of responsibility/information.
option_audit.C: Plausible chain-of-command shortcut; incorrect because indirect relay and delayed clarification do not provide the strongest handoff between sending and receiving clinicians.
option_audit.D: Plausible procedure-focused report; incorrect because it omits current condition, recent changes, response, and ongoing plan.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on only/all/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 146, B 153, C 138, D 138 characters; the correct answer is not the longest and choices are substantially balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives describe realistic transfer/handoff workflows rather than obviously unsafe caricatures.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. B lacks confirmed/direct handoff, C relies on indirect relay and delayed clarification, and D omits essential current/ongoing information. Post-fetch adversarial reread remains required.
